questions.question: When driving on major highways, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On highways, you must stay alert and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. Avoid looking at one thing for more than a few seconds. Keep moving your eyes to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down and look for a train. Be ready to stop. If red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to drive around the gate.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect your driving ability. Worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness can reduce your concentration. If you feel emotionally unstable, it is better to wait before driving.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while under the influence of alcohol or drugs is a serious safety problem. Safe driving is impossible when impaired. Drinking and driving endangers you and everyone else on the road.

questions.question: Why can night driving be more difficult than daytime driving?

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far. Always use proper headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They provide information for drivers.
They are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers position their vehicles correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn of upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Drivers should keep a safe distance from cyclists.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Always maintain a safe distance between your vehicle and cyclists.

questions.question: What should you do when merging into a crowded freeway?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to reach the speed of freeway traffic. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure you have enough space to merge safely.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you a false sense of confidence.
It impairs your thinking ability.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, impairs your coordination, and reduces your ability to judge distance. Your vision and thinking become worse after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: Smoking and getting ready to smoke while driving:

options.text: Do not affect your ability to drive.
Help keep you alert while driving.
Are distracting activities.
Are not distracting activities.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous because it makes you take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger tells you something different.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if the area were not under construction.

questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to. Not following their directions is illegal and dangerous for construction workers.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on the left.
Keep driving when you think most children have exited the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm out. Do not move until the stop arm is raised.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are just suggestions.
Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and tell drivers about road conditions. You must always obey them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
These lanes are reserved for buses and cars with a driver and at least one passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can happen when:

options.text: You stare at the road for long periods of time.
You stop to rest frequently.
You get too much sleep the night before your trip.
You take short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without looking around. You zone out and may not see traffic that is slowing down or stopping ahead of you, which can cause a crash.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under any railroad gate or barrier.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A deaf person.
A person doing a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must give the right-of-way to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to get rid of the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to get rid of the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers can help you stay awake, but they do not lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: Drivers may not park:

options.text: In front of mailboxes.
On bridges.
In highway tunnels.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: There are many places where parking is not allowed. These include in front of mailboxes, in front of driveways, in tunnels, and on bridges.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way road.
No right turn.
Exit.
Sharp right turn ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves sharply to the right.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By staring straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane.

questions.question: Cell phones can be a serious source of driver distractions.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You should not use cell phones while driving. Keep your full attention on the road. Only use your phone to report a crash or emergency.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing:

options.text: As long as an approaching train is not too close.
If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
If you first look carefully in both directions.
Under no circumstances.

questions.explanation: When you see flashing red lights, lowered gates, or bells at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Never drive around or under a moving gate. Wait until the lights stop and the gates are fully raised.

questions.question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane show the boundaries of a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians are responsible to stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Call the police immediately.
Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know he is wrong.
Use a driving action of your own to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not try to get even, as this makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive with your flashers on.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You are driving on the roadway and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, slow down and pull over to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: The most effective thing you can do to reduce your risk of being injured or killed in a traffic crash is to:

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the best way to protect yourself from death or injury in a crash.
